page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 10.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, equating to 2.62 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 24 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside AES acceleration. The server lacks attached local storage and includes no discrete graphics hardware, relying on external network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, supported by a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate entry-to-moderate computational and throughput levels. In CPU evaluation suites, the system scored 1406.1 in stress-ng single-core and 3689.06 in multi-core metrics, aligning with its dual-core physical topology. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1133.0 and a multi-core score of 2509.0, reflecting lower-quartile performance relative to larger or newer architectures. Memory throughput metrics include a read bandwidth of 25.89 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 23.1 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, though the PassMark memory score registered at 1031.78. LLM token generation on a 135M model achieved an average rating of 75.07 tokens per second, while larger parameter models are unsupported by the available memory footprint.

The c5n.xlarge configuration offers a balance suited for cost-conscious, compute-focused workloads that require enhanced network capabilities over standard baseline compute tiers. The inclusion of 5 Gbps baseline networking makes it viable for intermediate data ingestion, web serving pipelines, and networked microservices. However, the limitation of 2 physical cores and 10.0 GB of RAM prevents it from handling large database environments or heavy multi-threaded data science operations. The server is primarily suitable for network-bound utilities, moderate static web serving, code compilation tasks, and lightweight distributed application workers.
